details: CONFIRMED by a repro (below). relay_config.ROOT is abspath, not realpath; main_checkout returns
os.path.dirname(os.path.realpath(common)). Today /Users/amidman/relay is a real folder, so no effect on the owner's machine;
it matters if an install ever reaches relay through a symlink or RELAY_ROOT names one. The same asymmetry is in master's
evidence: python3 -I with lib/ on sys.path, a temp repo R/real, symlink R/link, worktree R/real/.worktrees/x:
failing_case: Main checkout at R/real, reached as R/link (symlink); linked worktree R/real/.worktrees/x.
So a global file written from a worktree and then checked from the main checkout reads as stale (and the reverse), and each
sync flips it. Both paths stay valid, so nothing points at a removed folder; only the drift check and rewrites are affected.
It should produce the same path from both.
fix_hint: Resolve both sides the same way: named = os.path.join(relay_setup.main_checkout(ROOT) or os.path.realpath(ROOT), "rules"),
and update test_full_text_paths_in_the_main_checkout_are_unchanged to expect the resolved path; or leave as is and drop it.
pass_cases: 1. ROOT = R/link (symlink to the main checkout) and ROOT = R/link/.worktrees/x: rules()["a"]["path"] is the same string.
2. ROOT = a plain main checkout (no symlink): path == os.path.join(ROOT, "rules", "a.md") as today.
3. ROOT = a linked worktree of a plain checkout: path == <main checkout>/rules/a.md (the current test).
reason: tests/test_rules.py test_a_symlinked_main_checkout_gives_the_same_path_as_its_worktree passes; fails at 916fbc6. Fix: relay_rules.py realpath fallback.
findings.summary: the main checkout's path is resolved (realpath) only when rendered from a worktree, so a main checkout reached through a symlink renders different paths from the main checkout and from its worktrees
